intelligence.enrichment: As the Moon revolves around Earth, a lunar eclipse can occur when Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon; a total lunar eclipse occurs when the Moon is completely in Earth's shadow. Earth between the Sun's light and the Moon blocks sunlight from the Moon, making Earth's shadow appear on the Moon's disc. The learner correctly applies this rule: As the Moon revolves around Earth, a lunar eclipse can occur when Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon; a total lunar eclipse occurs when the Moon is completely in Earth's shadow. A lunar eclipse is the Moon blocking the Sun or making its own shadow.

spec.instruction: Write one new grades 7 Science question. Chapter: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky. The student must decide: A lunar eclipse occurs when Earth blocks sunlight from reaching the Moon and Earth's shadow falls on the Moon. Use an Indian school or home setting and Indian names. Keep the source language register. Change the numbers, materials, or everyday situation. Do not copy the source stem. Recalculate the key. Do not print mix-up labels, hinge codes, node codes, or the word CANDIDATE.
